title: CHARM+: Cross-Hardware Attention with Re-Merge Multistream Mechanism
claim: Shared links cause contention and blocking when many transfers run at once; dedicated switched links let concurrent transfers proceed unblocked.
layout: 2 panels, side-by-side, left-to-right; color-coded lines for communication, idle and contention
description: Two panels compare GPU interconnects. Panel (a) on the left shows two NUMA nodes. Each has a CPU box above a PCIe switch (a dashed beige region), and four GPUs sit below it. Many parallel bus lines run through the switch. In NUMA0 the blue arrows from GPU0 to GPU1 show communication, and gray lines show idle links. In NUMA1 red arrows from GPU4 to GPU7 pile up on the shared bus, which marks contention. A legend at the top maps blue to communication, gray to idle and red to contention. Panel (b) on the right shows eight GPUs on top, fully connected by thin lines to four NVSwitch boxes at the bottom. Thick blue lines mark several simultaneous communications on dedicated links. The captions below read 'Blocking comm due to link contention in PCIe' and 'Non-blocking comm on dedicated links in NVLink'. The eye goes first to the red bundle of contended arrows.
caption: Communication under PCIe and NVLink. The left of (a) shows single communication at full bandwidth without contention, while the right shows multiple communications at limited bandwidth with contention. (b) shows multiple communications at full bandwidth without contention.
abstract: As sequence lengths continue to grow, distributed attention based on sequence parallel (e.g., Ring-Attention) has become a mainstream solution for large language models (LLMs). Nevertheless, inherent communication dependencies limit computation-communication overlap, reducing GPU utilization. Moreover, in cross-hardware (NUMA or node) architectures, due to imbalanced communication bandwidth, frequent communication synchronization will limit overall performance. Based on these insights, we propose CHARM+, Cross-Hardware Attention with Re-Merge Multistream Mechanism. We reorganize sequential communications into several levels and achieve intra-level parallelism and computation overlap. Furthermore, we decouple cross-hardware communication from intra-hardware communication, eliminating synchronization overhead caused by bandwidth imbalance. Forward and backward algorithms were evaluated on multiple hardware architectures and consistently outperformed state-of-the-art methods. Compared to Ring-Attention, our forward and backward algorithms achieve average speedups of 1.3x and 1.7x on a dual-NUMA PCIe architecture, and 2.8x and 2.9x on a dual-node NVLink architecture, respectively.
